Incident Bot: [SEV2] routing anomaly detected — unexpected hosted routing for tenants normally pinned to Dedicated pool. spike in cross-tenant error rates. auto-runbook triggered: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2034567890/runbook :rotating_light:

Ryan (oncall): seeing it, paging SRE. which region?

Anya SRE: eu-west-1 primarily, but a handful in us-east-1. request rate to hosted shot up 4x for dedicated-tier customers starting 02:03 UTC.

Maya (eng-runtime): logs show policy eval path: `if capacity_tier == "dedicated" then route->dedicated_pool else hosted` — but there's an override flag `force_hosted_on_threshold=true` that was rolled out in canary last night. suspect threshold logic lower than intended.

Jun (routing): also noticed `tenant_shard_key` was missing in the routing context for some requests (K8s sidecar update dropped header). that combined with override means requests matched a fallback rule that maps to hosted default -> tenant isolation bypassed.

Infra Bot: alert: 12 dedicated-bound tenants currently routed to hosted default pool. 3 tenant error spikes > 5% 503s.

Ryan (oncall): immediate mitigations — stop canary, revert override, and add temporary reject rule at edge to prevent dedicated-tenant IDs routing to hosted. I'll coordinate.

Maya (eng-runtime): rolling rollback of feature flag `force_hosted_on_threshold` now -> `ff toggle --off force_hosted_on_threshold --env prod`. patching in progress.

Anya SRE: while rollback runs, advise adding an explicit rule: `route.policy.insert(0, deny if capacity_tier=="dedicated" AND route_target=="hosted_default")` on routing-control-plane. I'll apply.

Jun (routing): applying deny rule now. command:```
POST /api/v1/policies/insert
{"rule": "deny", "match": "tier==dedicated && dest==hosted_default", "reason": "temp-mitigation-2034567890"}
```

Support: impacted customers observed — acct 3482, acct 9001, acct-mlplatform reported latency and auth errors. sending note to CS to open incident tickets.

Infra Bot: deny rule accepted, 10s propagation to edge. rollback flag toggle succeeded on all regions.

Ryan (oncall): monitoring metrics: hosted ingress for those tenant ids dropping back to baseline. Anya — verify KV cache keys weren't poisoned by cross-tenant entries?

Anya SRE: good catch — KV cache had 8 keys with mixed tenant prefix for the hosted default backend. flushing cache for affected shards: `cachectl flush --shard eu-west-1 --prefix tenant:` done.

Jun (routing): double-checked routing logs after deny: no new cross-bindings. request path now includes tenant_shard_key again.

Maya (eng-runtime): running quick smoke on model variants: some requests that hit hosted used smaller model variant (quantized) unexpectedly because model-variant mapping was part of the fallback policy. that's why some customers saw quality regressions. patching mapping to prefer equivalent variant in hosted-only as temporary.

Ryan (oncall): summary so far: root cause = combination of (1) canary flag lowered threshold allowing fallback, (2) sidecar release dropped tenant_shard header for some flows, (3) fallback policy mapped to hosted_default without tenant isolation. Impact = subset of dedicated customers routed to hosted causing errors + quality regressions. Mitigations = rollback flag, deny rule, cache flush, variant mapping patch.

Support: notifying affected customers now with ETA ~20m, offering post-incident credits if regression confirmed.

Anya SRE: raising pager to SEV1 if errors don't stabilize in 10m. current trend improving.

Ryan (oncall): handoff to Maya for post-stabilization cleanup. I'm marking incident in-flight and creating incident channel.

Maya (eng-runtime): taking over. action items: collect full routing trace for 02:00-02:10 UTC, validate flag rollout logs, repro the missing header scenario, tighten fallback policy grammar to require tenant_shard match, and schedule postmortem.

Jun (routing): will create PR to make fallback policy require `tenant_shard_key` and add unit tests.

Support: customers notified, one replied "thanks for quick fix".

Incident Bot: incident state -> mitigated. watch for regressions for 24h. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2034567890/postmortem

Maya (eng-runtime): creating postmortem draft and timeline, will tag owners for follow-ups: flag rollback validation (Maya), sidecar release revert and fix (Jun), policy hardening (Anya), customer outreach postmortem (Support).

Ryan (oncall): thumbs up. leaving notes in the incident doc. handing to oncall rotation team for 24h watch. :white_check_mark:
